advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a behavioral test that executes the 'Fetch full code ref history' step (fake git on PATH, like the pack-guard tests) for GITHUB_REF values refs/heads/feature/x, refs/pull/123/merge, and a bare ref, asserting the concrete refspec passed to git fetch and the shallow-vs-non-shallow branch taken.
evidence: Test only greps script text: `assert "refs/heads/*" in script`, `assert "refs/pull/*" in script`, `assert "+${GITHUB_REF}:${dest_ref}" in script` (tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py:100-105)

Workflow branch under test computes distinct dest_refs: `refs/pull/*) dest_ref="refs/remotes/origin/${GITHUB_REF#refs/}" ;;` and `refs/heads/*) dest_ref="refs/remotes/origin/${GITHUB_REF#refs/heads/}" ;;` (.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml:66-69)

The shallow/non-shallow branch (`if [ "$(git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository)" = "true" ]; then ... --unshallow ... else ... fi`, .github/workflows/verify-identity.yml:71-75) is never exercised; only the substring `--unshallow` is grepped, so the else branch is untested.

ABSENCE: the same test module executes the pack guard for real via `subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", _standalone_guard(...)])` (lines 217-219, 233-235), showing these run: scripts are executable and behavior-testable, yet the new fetch step is only text-grepped.

Named violating inputs left uncaught: GITHUB_REF=refs/pull/123/merge (expected dest_ref refs/remotes/origin/pull/123/merge) and GITHUB_REF=refs/heads/feature/x (expected dest_ref refs/remotes/origin/feature/x); a wrong-prefix strip would keep every substring assertion green.
advisory.finding: The new branch logic in the 'Fetch full code ref history' step (the `case "$GITHUB_REF"` computing dest_ref for refs/heads/*, refs/pull/*, and default, plus the shallow/non-shallow --unshallow conditional) is verified only by static substring greps over the script text, not by executing it, so a regression in the dest_ref computation is undetectable.
scenarios: A future edit changes `${GITHUB_REF#refs/heads/}` to a wrong expansion, producing a malformed dest_ref refspec, but all grep assertions still pass.
The non-shallow else branch fetch is broken; no test drives GITHUB_REF through a non-shallow repo, so the regression ships.
advisory.suggested_fix: Follow the existing pack-guard pattern: run the normalized step script under `bash -c` with a fake `git` that records its argv, parametrize over GITHUB_REF in {refs/heads/feature/x, refs/pull/123/merge, HEAD}, and assert the recorded fetch refspec equals the expected `+${GITHUB_REF}:${dest_ref}` value and that --unshallow appears only when git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository is stubbed true.
